transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-12-18
Start: 16:32 PST
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Meyers (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (Ironwood Head of Platform), Sana Khan (AI Eng), Evan Ortiz (CTO)

Auto-generated Summary (may be imperfect):
Ironwood wants a quick way to move from prototype to production with minimal infra effort. They want to try Redwood hosted quickstart with credits but are evaluating Dedicated/Private for data residency and encryption in future. Security and auditability flagged as must-haves; TTFT expectations around 200-600ms for 256 tokens were mentioned but somewhat fuzzy.

Transcript Body:
00:00 Jordan: Alright hey everyone thanks for making time, um this is Jordan Meyers from Redwood Inference. I'm joined by Priya my solutions engineer. Today we wanted to understand what Ironwood's sprint goals are and what you need to get to "first live inference".
00:10 Marcus: Yep thanks Jordan, Marcus here. We have a small squad trying to add semantic search and a chat assist to our admin portal. Goal is to get something into an internal beta in the next 3 weeks. We're trying to decide whether to just use the hosted API with your free credits or go straight to a dedicated pilot.
00:25 Jordan: Totally. Quick q — when you say "first live inference" do you mean in prod or in a staging environment that we can give you lower SLAs for?
00:32 Marcus: Staging first, but it needs to mirror prod in security posture. Our security team won't accept lax audit logs.
00:37 Priya: Got it. For staging you'd normally take the self-serve hosted flow; we provide a quickstart with credits that gets you to first token in under an hour for most teams. The dedicated option is typically chosen when you have predictable throughput or stricter data isolation needs.
00:52 Sana: Quick clarifying q — what does Redwood mean by "data isolation" on Dedicated? Is it a VPC endpoint or like full air-gap?
01:00 Priya: Good question. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and VPC peering + private networking. Private on-prem is our fully customer-managed package for air-gapped environments. There's some nuance around control plane v data plane but we can unpack that in the security call.
01:15 Evan: Are audit logs easily exportable? We need all token-level logs and request/response hashes into our SIEM.
01:22 Jordan: Yes we support audit logs and structured tracing. We can stream logs to your SaaS SIEM or via S3/KMS encrypted buckets; we'll validate retention policy too.
01:30 Marcus: What's the typical TTFT for teams doing the quickstart? We care because our UX folks measure time-to-first-meaningful-token not just connect time.
01:38 Priya: For most teams on hosted it's minutes to first API key and seconds to first request. For meaningful response — depends on prompt and model size. For small to medium prompts (256 tokens) you should expect 200-900ms per token on our low-latency hosted path we call Redwood Fast — erm sorry internal name got mangled in meet, but basically our fast path — and we can show sample numbers.
01:55 Jordan: We'll share a short benchmark sheet, Priya will run 512 token baseline for the sample model you mentioned.
02:00 Marcus: Great. Another constraint — we have a regulatory customer in EMEA and need to ensure data residency. If we go hosted, can we pin region?
02:08 Priya: Yes, hosted supports regional endpoints. For full data residency guarantees, customers often go Dedicated in a single region or Private. But the hosted product does allow region pinning for requests.
02:18 Sana: What's the cost delta between hosted and dedicated for small scale? We don't have huge QPS yet, but if costs explode when we scale we'll need a plan.
02:28 Jordan: Hosted is usage-based, so up front it's cheapest for low volume. Dedicated has a monthly commitment but predictable unit costs and isolation. We can run a TCO comparison for your expected QPS.
02:38 Marcus: We're evaluating a couple of competitors too. We looked at Anthropic's hosted endpoint and also internal on-prem experiments.
02:45 Evan: Are there model version pinning and rollout features? We need to be able to roll back if a model regression happens.
02:51 Priya: Yes, our Console supports model pinning, canary rollouts and automatic fallback to a cheaper/older variant. It's in the rollout section, we'll share screenshots.
03:00 Jordan: For your time-to-first-token objective, most teams follow the quickstart script: redeem credits, spin up API key, run a smoke test with sample prompt, evaluate latency and quality, then decide if you need dedicated pilot.
03:12 Marcus: That flow sounds good. For the quickstart we need a step-by-step doc and a set of prompts so our QA can validate outputs deterministically.
03:20 Jordan: We'll include a starter prompt set and an eval harness in the playbook.
03:25 Sana: On security: SAML SSO, RBAC, KMS integration are must-haves, and we want proof of SOC 2 Type II or equivalent.
03:34 Priya: We have SOC 2 and can share the attestation. SSO via SAML, RBAC roles in Console and KMS/HSM integrations for private deployments are supported. For hosted we can integrate with your KMS for object storage encryption and provide customer-managed keys in some plans.
03:52 Evan: If we do a quickstart on hosted and then decide to go dedicated, how seamless is migration?
03:58 Priya: You can pin models and move traffic; we support automated data plane migrations in most cases. The biggest work is network configuration and possibly model quantization differences. We'll outline migration steps in the playbook.
04:10 Marcus: One more — we do a lot of caching at the prefix level internally, does Redwood provide KV cache hooks or prefix caching?
04:18 Priya: Yes we support prefix caching and persistent KV cache for session workloads. You can configure TTLs and cache layers in the runtime. Sometimes docs transcribe that as "K-V cash" but it's KV cache.
04:30 Jordan: Okay quick recap — you're fine to start with hosted quickstart to validate product UX, you need credits and playbook, you want a 512-token latency baseline from Priya, and security follow-up around SAML/KMS/audit logs. Anything else?\04:43 Marcus: Could you include an example of a canary rollout config?
04:46 Priya: Yep we'll attach a sample canary policy and the Console screenshot.
04:50 Evan: Also please note we need the pricing bracket for sustained 10k requests/day as that's our expected pilot peak.
04:56 Jordan: We'll include a cost estimate row for that QPS in the TCO sheet.
05:00 Marcus: Awesome, that covers the main stuff.
05:03 Jordan: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the playbook and bench results.

Occasional transcription glitches observed during call: "Redwood Fast" referred to as "Redwood Fast path" and once as "Redwood fast-pastry"; "KV cache" heard as "K V cash"; "canary" sometimes transcribed as "canary-flag"; speaker labels briefly switched (Sana tagged as "Speaker 4" in system export).

Meeting close & explicit next steps recap:
- Jordan: Send quickstart playbook + redemption link for credits (due 12/20).
- Priya: Run latency baseline for 512 tokens on hosted and share spreadsheet + suggested config (due 12/22).
- Marcus: Share list of 3 endpoints and peak QPS for pilot (due 12/24).
- Schedule security deep-dive between Ironwood infra and Redwood security (Proposed dates included in follow-up email).

Links referenced during call (representative):
- Quickstart playbook (link to Redwood quickstart)
- Sample canary rollout screenshot (Console)

End of transcript.
